goal: Blink an LED on an Arduino Uno: one red 5 mm LED on pin D13 through a 220 ohm resistor to GND, on for one second and off for one second.

plan.title: Blink one red LED with Arduino Uno
plan.summary: Build a circuit with one red LED controlled by Arduino pin D13. A 220 ohm resistor limits the LED current, and the sketch turns the LED on for one second and off for one second, repeatedly.
plan.final_result: The finished circuit has one red LED across rows 10 and 11, one 220 ohm resistor from row 11 to row 15, and exactly three jumper wires. With the supplied sketch loaded and the Uno powered through USB, the external LED lights for one second, goes dark for one second, and repeats. The Uno's built-in D13 indicator may blink too.
safety: Keep the Uno disconnected from USB and other power while placing or changing components.
Always keep the 220 ohm resistor in series with the LED; never connect the LED directly between D13 and GND.
Check the LED polarity and exact holes before applying power, and never connect an Arduino power pin directly to GND.
Bend component leads gently and avoid letting exposed leads touch neighbouring connections.

part_guide.breadboard: The white board with numbered rows and lettered holes holds connections without soldering. Holes a–e within one numbered row are connected internally.
part_guide.uno: The blue-green Arduino Uno has black pin sockets and a large USB socket. Its D13 output controls this LED, and GND provides the return connection.
part_guide.red_led: The red, rounded lamp has a longer positive leg and a shorter negative leg; the negative side also has a flat edge on the flange. It is the light that blinks.
part_guide.led_resistor: The small tan component has red, red, brown, and usually gold bands. It limits LED current and can face either direction.
part_guide.ground_feed: This black jumper runs from the Uno socket labelled GND to the first hole of the top ground rail. It connects that rail to Arduino ground.
part_guide.led_signal: This yellow jumper runs from the Uno socket labelled 13 to row 10. It carries the on/off signal to the LED's longer leg.
part_guide.led_ground: This black jumper runs straight from row 15 to the ground rail above it. It completes the LED's return path through the resistor.

assumptions: No existing components or placements were stated, so all required parts are marked as added.
The outer rail above column a is the blue-marked ground (-) rail along the top edge; no positive rail is needed.
Breadboard holes a–e at the same row number are connected internally.
The Uno uses the required simplified 55 × 28 × 7 mm scene template; its actual PCB is 68.6 × 53.4 × 1.6 mm, and pin anchors are symbolic.
The resistor is on the LED cathode side to follow the specified wiring pattern; a series resistor limits current on either side of an LED.
A computer with Arduino programming software is available; choose a USB data cable whose computer-end plug fits that computer.
